symptom: Two PCs both plugged into SW1 in Room 204 cannot ping each other even though both report IPs in 192.168.10.0/24.
topology_note: SW1 access ports Fa0/5 (PC-A) and Fa0/6 (PC-B) should both be in VLAN 10 (Sales).
show_output:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/7
10   Sales                            active    Fa0/5
20   Engineering                      active    Fa0/6, Fa0/8

SW1# show interfaces fa0/5 switchport
Name: Fa0/5
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (Sales)

SW1# show interfaces fa0/6 switchport
Name: Fa0/6
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (Engineering)
expected_fault: PC-B's port Fa0/6 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, so the two PCs are on different broadcast domains despite matching IP subnet config.

IP Address......: 192.168.10.15

Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol

expected_fault: PC-C's configured default gateway 192.168.10.254 does not match the router subinterface address 192.168.10.1, so all off-subnet traffic has nowhere to go.

symptom: Entire VLAN 40 subnet lost internet access simultaneously; internal same-VLAN traffic still works.
topology_note: R2's Gi0/1.40 subinterface is the gateway for 192.168.40.0/24.

interface GigabitEthernet0/1.40
 encapsulation dot1Q 40

symptom: PC-D can ping its own gateway but nothing beyond it; a duplicate IP warning appeared briefly on boot.
topology_note: 192.168.30.1 should be uniquely assigned to R1 Gi0/0.30 only.

PC-D> ipconfig
IP Address......: 192.168.30.1
Subnet Mask......: 255.255.255.0

Interface               IP-Address      OK? Method Status  Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0.30     192.168.30.1    YES manual up      up
expected_fault: PC-D was statically assigned 192.168.30.1, the same address as the router's own gateway interface, creating an IP conflict that breaks routing for that host.

symptom: PC-E can reach the gateway and other subnets, but a specific server report is intermittently unreachable.
topology_note: PC-E and the file server 192.168.50.20 are both meant to sit on 192.168.50.0/24.

Interface               IP-Address      OK? Method Status  Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/2.50     192.168.50.1    YES manual up      up
expected_fault: PC-E's subnet mask (255.255.0.0) does not match the router's /24 configuration, causing PC-E to think the server is locally reachable via ARP when it actually needs routing, producing intermittent failures.

Pool SALES-POOL :
 Network         : 192.168.20.0 /24
 Default router  : 192.168.10.1
 Lease time      : 1 days

R1# show ip dhcp binding
(no bindings)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool SALES-POOL is configured for the wrong network (192.168.20.0 instead of 192.168.10.0), so it never leases addresses to VLAN 10 clients, which fall back to APIPA.

symptom: About half of VLAN 40 PCs get IP addresses fine; the rest fail DHCP intermittently during the morning rush.

IP address       Detection method   Detection time
192.168.40.61     Ping                Aug 20 2026 09:14

symptom: All PCs in the Engineering Lab fail DHCP and show no IP at all, even though the pool config looks correct.
topology_note: R1 should have 'service dhcp' enabled globally and Gi0/0.30 should not be excluded from DHCP relay.

no service dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAB-POOL
 network 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.30.1
expected_fault: The DHCP service is globally disabled ('no service dhcp'), so the router ignores all DISCOVER broadcasts regardless of the pool configuration.

 Network         : 192.168.50.0 /24
 Default router  : 192.168.50.1

symptom: PC-F can ping 8.8.8.8 successfully but 'ping google.com' fails with 'Unknown host'.

expected_fault: PC-F has no DNS server configured (0.0.0.0), so name resolution fails while raw IP connectivity works fine - a classic Layer 7 vs Layer 3 split.

symptom: PC-H resolves internal hostnames fine but every external domain lookup times out.

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 can reach VLAN 20 but cannot reach VLAN 30 (Engineering Lab) at all.

     192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
     192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20

R1# show running-config | include interface Gi
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
expected_fault: No subinterface or route exists for the 192.168.30.0/24 (VLAN 30) network, so the router has no way to forward traffic there.

symptom: Branch office (192.168.60.0/24 via R2) cannot reach HQ subnet 192.168.10.0/24; HQ can reach the branch fine.
topology_note: R2 needs a static route back to 192.168.10.0/24 via its WAN link 10.10.10.1.
show_output:
R2# show ip route
S*   0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 10.10.10.1
     192.168.60.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
     10.10.10.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0

R2# show running-config | include ip route
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.10.10.1
expected_fault: R2 only has a default route toward the WAN, but the HQ side has a specific route back to the branch, creating asymmetric routing - the return path from HQ to branch works but R2 never learns a path to 192.168.10.0/24 explicitly. The missing explicit or default route on the HQ router is the actual gap.

symptom: After a router reload, all inter-VLAN routing in the Engineering Lab stopped; interfaces show up/up.
topology_note: R1 should be running 'ip routing' globally to route between subinterfaces.
show_output:

Interface               IP-Address      OK? Method Status  Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0.10     192.168.10.1    YES manual up      up
GigabitEthernet0/0.30     192.168.30.1    YES manual up      up

R1# show running-config | include ip routing
no ip routing
expected_fault: Global IP routing was disabled on the router (likely reset by the reload picking up a saved config), so it no longer routes between its own subinterfaces despite them being up.

symptom: Library Annex (192.168.50.0/24) has full connectivity to everything except one remote subnet 172.16.5.0/24 used by a partner lab.
topology_note: A static route to 172.16.5.0/24 should point via next-hop 192.168.99.2.
show_output:

     192.168.50.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/2
     192.168.99.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/1/0
S    172.16.5.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.99.20
expected_fault: The static route to 172.16.5.0/24 was entered with the wrong next-hop (192.168.99.20 instead of 192.168.99.2), a typo one octet off from the correct value, so packets are sent to a non-existent neighbor.

symptom: VLAN 10 PCs can reach everything except the HR server 192.168.99.10, which times out for all users including HR staff.

show_output:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
    10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.99.10 (234 matches)
    20 permit ip any any (890 matches)

R1# show ip interface gi0/0.10 | include access list
  Outgoing access list is not set
  Inbound  access list is 101
expected_fault: ACL 101's first line denies all of 192.168.10.0/24 to the HR server with no exception carved out for the HR staff subnet (192.168.10.100-110), so the ACL is simply too broad.

symptom: Marketing VLAN 40 users report that internal email works but they cannot reach any website (HTTP/HTTPS).
topology_note: ACL 110 on R2 should permit TCP 80/443 outbound from 192.168.40.0/24 to any.
show_output:
R2# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
    10 permit tcp 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 25 (1200 matches)
    20 permit tcp 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 110 (600 matches)
    30 deny ip any any (5400 matches)
expected_fault: ACL 110 only explicitly permits SMTP (25) and POP3 (110) before the implicit/explicit deny-any, with no line allowing TCP 80 or 443, so all web traffic is silently dropped.

symptom: Engineering Lab (VLAN 30) users cannot ping the gateway or anything else; they had access yesterday.
topology_note: ACL 120 should only restrict Telnet/SSH management access, not general traffic, on Gi0/0.30.
show_output:
R1# show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
    10 deny ip any any (15400 matches)

R1# show ip interface gi0/0.30 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 120
expected_fault: ACL 120 as currently written is a single 'deny ip any any' with no permit statements at all, blocking every packet inbound on Gi0/0.30 - likely an incomplete ACL that was applied before the permit lines were added.

symptom: Guest laptops in the Library Annex can reach the internet but are also able to reach the internal staff file server, which should be blocked.
topology_note: ACL 130 should deny Library-Guest (192.168.55.0/24) access to staff server 192.168.50.20 specifically.
show_output:
R3# show access-lists 130
Extended IP access list 130
    10 permit ip 192.168.55.0 0.0.0.255 any (3400 matches)

R3# show ip interface gi0/3 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 130
expected_fault: ACL 130 only contains a blanket permit for the guest subnet with no deny rule for the staff server, so the intended isolation between guest and staff networks was never actually implemented.

symptom: No internal PC can reach the internet even though the default route and ISP link both show up/up.
topology_note: R1 should NAT-overload 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 out Gi0/1 (the ISP-facing interface).
show_output:
R1# show ip nat translations
(no translations)

R1# show running-config | include nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
access-list 1 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255

R1# show ip interface gi0/0.10 | include NAT
  NAT is not enabled on this interface
expected_fault: The 'ip nat inside' designation was never applied to Gi0/0.10 (or any internal interface), so even though the NAT overload rule exists, the router doesn't know which interfaces are 'inside' to translate.

symptom: Marketing VLAN 40 can browse the internet fine; Sales VLAN 10 at the same branch cannot.
topology_note: NAT ACL 1 should permit both 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.40.0/24 for overload translation.
show_output:
R2# show running-config | include access-list 1
access-list 1 permit 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255

R2# show ip nat translations
Pro  Inside global      Inside local       Outside local      Outside global
tcp  203.0.113.5:1024   192.168.40.10:1024  93.184.216.34:80   93.184.216.34:80
expected_fault: NAT access-list 1 only includes the 192.168.40.0/24 network; the 192.168.10.0/24 (Sales) network was never added, so Sales traffic has no matching translation rule and is dropped at the NAT boundary.

symptom: Internet access for the Engineering Lab works for a while each morning, then stops until the router is reloaded.
topology_note: R1 uses NAT overload on a single ISP-facing interface; no NAT pool with static entries is configured.
show_output:
R1# show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 0 (0 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)
Peak translations: 4096, occurred 0:42:10 ago
Expired translations: 51200

R1# show ip nat translations
(no translations)
expected_fault: The NAT translation table hit its peak capacity (4096) and expired entries aren't being cleared fast enough under load, exhausting available port/address combinations until a reload clears the table - a NAT overload capacity/timeout issue rather than a config typo.

symptom: External partner cannot initiate a connection to the internally hosted library catalog server on its public-facing NAT address.
topology_note: A static NAT entry should map public 203.0.113.20 to internal library server 192.168.50.30 port 80.
show_output:
R3# show ip nat translations
Pro  Inside global         Inside local        Outside local  Outside global
---  203.0.113.20          192.168.50.3        ---            ---

R3# show running-config | include nat
ip nat inside source static 192.168.50.3 203.0.113.20
expected_fault: The static NAT entry points to 192.168.50.3 instead of the actual library server at 192.168.50.30 - a typo missing the trailing digit - so inbound connections are forwarded to the wrong (likely nonexistent) internal host.

symptom: Laptops can see the 'CorpNet' SSID and associate, but authentication fails every time with the correct password.
